feature: A dropped capture lands where you let go of it
summary: Dragging a picture onto the canvas now leaves it centred on the point you let go of, instead of jumping to the middle of the canvas. A picture too big for the canvas is still scaled down to fit, but it sits around the drop point rather than dead centre.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Nothing to turn on. You need at least one capture on the Library shelf (open the right hand dock, Library, Media).

try.do: Make a new blank canvas, roughly 900 by 700.
Open the Library shelf in the right hand dock and pick Media.
Drag a small capture off the shelf and let go near the top right of the white canvas.
Read X and Y in Position & Size: the picture is centred on the spot you let go of.
Drag the same file in from a Finder window and let go somewhere else. It lands the same way.
Drag one more in and let go a few points inside the top left corner: it is nudged wholly onto the canvas, never half off.
Drag in a screenshot bigger than the canvas and let go high up: it is scaled down to fit, sitting high rather than centred.
Press Command V with an image on the clipboard: a paste has no pointer, so it still arrives in the middle.

evaluate: When you let go, does the picture appear where your eye already was?
Nudging a picture wholly onto the canvas when you let go over the edge: helpful, or would you rather it hung off the edge exactly where you dropped it?
A picture too big for the canvas can only shift a little before it runs out of room. Does that feel right, or does it read as the old jump-to-centre?
Should a paste keep landing in the middle, or should it land wherever you last clicked?
Nothing is drawn while the picture is in the air, so you cannot see how big it will land until you let go. How much does that bother you?
rough: There is no landing outline while a capture is being dragged over the canvas. A component dragged off the shelf draws the box it will fill; a picture draws nothing, so the size is a surprise until you let go. Filed as its own task rather than bundled in here.

Letting go over the canvas edge nudges the picture wholly onto the canvas instead of leaving it half off. That is a judgement call, made to match what already happens when you drop onto a screen. Moving a layer afterwards is not clamped, so you can still push it off the edge by hand.
Verified live in the probe app with Screen Recording granted: the three shots are real window captures, not offscreen renders.
